# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s159 (`%14`, 2026-09-09 13:08 → 13:27 AEST — the review-blocks seat, commissioned because Kam was waiting on the review) | **ALL 43 OPEN PRs PLACED — four blocks, one stated exception, one dependabot batch — and the arithmetic CLOSED against the open-PR universe (11+6+14+1=32 +1 +10 = 43, asserted programmatically) rather than asserted in prose.** Every block carries the four fields Kam's rule requires: stream parent, its PRs and tickets, the ONE pass that proves it with **measured** wall-clocks (Schemathesis 13.4 min / 2,016 cases, Playwright 3.8 s, k6 53 s, test:migrations ~40 s), and the single thing the human does — **with the unbaselined figures named as unbaselined instead of quietly inherited.** 🔴 **THE FINDING THAT PROTECTED KAM TODAY: #813 reads APPROVED, at-head and clean on every instrument, and Peter withdrew that approval IN WRITING four minutes after giving it.** `commit_id == head.sha` is blind to it by construction — that discriminator catches an approval the head moved PAST, and a withdrawn approval sits AT the head because the head never moved. **Swept across all 43, exactly two are this shape (#813, #785), so the headline "10 approved" is really 8.** Filed KS-1035. **Independently confirmed by Wednesday on Linear KS-791 before it reached Kam** — his two comments at 14:52:21Z and 14:56:21Z. **It corrected the coordinator's brief TWICE, with measurements:** there are FOUR stream parents not three, and the fourth (KS-485) is not findable by the title pattern the other three share — a discoverability trap it named for successors. And it **resolved the 14-vs-17-vs-20 disagreement from the census rather than picking a side**: 14 wired + 3 homed elsewhere + 3 deferred = 20 tracked, so the ticket's 17-of-20 and the handover's 14-of-20 were **both true about different things** — better than either source. **Item 1 delivered:** KS-926's work had NO PR at all; #918 opened with a Test Evidence block from its own runs. **And it reported its own instrument failing silently on the FIRST command of the session** — `timeout 90 git fetch | tail` on macOS, where `timeout` does not exist, so git never ran and the pipeline still exited 0. **Scope held exactly:** 0 merges · 0 deploys · 0 force pushes · 0 `--no-verify` · no rebase of branches under review (correctly refused as uncommissioned) · no contact with Peter or Stuart · no extranet post. | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Commissioned 13:08 on Kam's 13:05 *"will be going through the review as soon as its ready"*. Verified at rung 6 (named the brief, DKIM-verified it, negative control 4/4 · 0/9 · synthetic 9/9), not at the launcher's exit code. Wednesday's completion check: three commissioned items, three delivered, plus two findings beyond the commission; headline independently probed from the tracker. GO sent 13:29 for the rebases it offered (#866, #891, #880 + the named change on #887), mail verified at destination before the pointer tap. |

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
